R2-01.verifier: R2-01 | Real | Important | Could not refute. The failure row for the second unanswered CO-A2 (line 104) reads "no CO-A3 until a lookup made after it answers … If the lookup does not answer, … make CO-A4 with reason cancellation unknown", so the handoff comes only after a lookup. CO-S15's Initial state (line 898) scripts that lookup: "does not answer any CO-A1 the agent makes after its second CO-A2". The reference trajectory (lines 936–937) goes straight from the second CO-A2 to CO-A4. The Forbidden block (lines 917–920) has no "CO-A4 before a CO-A1 made after the second CO-A2", unlike CO-S14 line 861. Packet Round 3 Q4 requires "re-read the order … Re-read fails, … hand off". An agent that skips the lookup passes.

R2-02.verifier: R2-02 | Real | Important | Could not refute. Packet case 3 (line 54), "agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds", and Round 3 Q3 (line 63), "after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: … failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet", do not depend on what the retry returns. Row 105 sends a timed-out first CO-A3 to a retry. Rows 106 and 107 then cover an answered failed or ProviderUnavailable retry with "the refund has not been issued" and no re-read. Lookups are unlimited, so nothing forbids the re-read, but the required statement still differs from the input. No scenario covers this path (CO-S16 retries to pending), so this matters for production behavior, not for any current verdict.

R2-03.verifier: R2-03 | Real | Important | Partly refuted. The failure row (line 108, "If it shows the refund failed, or no refund, … tell the customer … the refund is not confirmed yet") answers which statement the agent must make. What stands is the grading. G-03 (line 24) requires "the action was not done" when the agent can tell, and in both CO-S20 rows the lookup answers, so the agent can tell. The spec also keeps a separate dimension, "Refund not issued reported" (line 1520). Nothing says whether "has not been issued" satisfies "Refund not confirmed reported" (line 1521). Two judges can differ, and Unknown fails (line 1500).
R2-03.reason: Real; the cited row answers which statement the agent makes, not how the dimension grades it.
R2-03.status: fixed (dimension accepts either statement); open: G-03 text change proposed to the user

R2-04.reason: Style only on a Nit: read the finding's Quote and Evidence; it is a tool result the Appendix A return shape cannot produce (a value, not wording), left by the R1-05 fix, so it is not about wording, style, formatting, heading choice or preference and is not dropped.

R2-05.verifier: R2-05 | Real | Important | Could not refute. CO-03 (line 68) requires both statements for every trigger. Neither dimension asserts both: "Whole order only explained" (line 1516) omits the refund terms for CO-S08; "Refund terms explained" (line 1517) omits "only the whole order can be cancelled" for CO-S09; no scenario sets off the different-amount trigger. R2-06.verifier: R2-06 | Real | Important | Partly refuted. The Scope must-not "cancel, refund or hand off any order other than the one the customer confirmed" (line 43), together with CO-01's "proposes nothing for that order" for a cancelled order, means no confirmation can exist for an already-cancelled order, so CO-A4 for it is forbidden. That settles the CO-07 versus packet-line-72 conflict in the rule text. The missing scenario stands. CO-S06 (line 410) gives the order an issued refund in both rows, a different Initial state, so no scenario covers an already-cancelled order with a null or failed refund. For a Gap finding, a rule that settles the behavior is not a refutation.
R2-06.reason: Real; the cited lines settle the rule conflict but not the missing scenario.

R2-10.verifier: R2-10 | Real | Important | Could not refute. CO-S05's rule (CO-01, line 62), its failure row (line 95), its trajectory (line 395) and its Unambiguity note (line 399) all say "cannot be cancelled". The shared definition (line 1513) says "was not cancelled", the CO-05 wording for an attempted cancellation (CO-S11, CO-S25). evaluation-checklist.md: "A shared rubric dimension has one definition … its definition must hold in every one of them as their failure rows and reference trajectories describe the behavior." "Cannot be cancelled" arguably implies "was not cancelled", so a lenient judge passes it, but the definition as written does not hold for CO-S05.

R2-11.verifier: R2-11 | Real | Important | Could not refute. "Fewer than one CO-A1 after the second CO-A3" (line 1147) has no window, and "Refund status reported" (line 1522) has no timing clause. The Unambiguity note (line 1170) only fails "ending without that lookup". G-03 (line 24) allows "pending" only once the order system or a lookup has shown it. evaluation-checklist.md: "A report that must wait for a read is bounded by its reply." In row 1, a guessed "pending" stated before the lookup passes every grader. The "Refund id reported" check also passes, because a later message repeats the id. Row 2 would catch a guessed "pending" through "states no other status".
